absent: AUSENTE: numeric values and sizing rationale for batch, generation, tier, zone, and history limits
AUSENTE: internals of folio lookup, young and dirty primitives, bloom filter, swappiness, protection, eviction, and sequence increment helpers
AUSENTE: full page-table walker contract including get_next_vma setup, PTE range walking, mm statistics indices, and notifier interaction

findings.text: One globally visible helper performs bounded look-around around a mapped address to refresh recency for nearby mappings while the caller already holds the page table lock.

Look-around entry scans PTEs within the intersection of the current PMD span and the VMA, capped to a bounded batch centered or clamped around the fault address. It clears young state with notifier awareness, skips single-page spans and special mappings, coalesces consecutive entries belonging to the same folio while tracking dirtiness, reports each distinct folio once to the generation walker, and feeds back to a per-mm bloom filter when the observed young density makes the PMD worth revisiting.

Huge PMD handling batches at most a small fixed number of entries using a first address plus a bitmap. The first encounter only arms the batch, nearby offsets set bitmap bits, and a distant address or explicit terminator flushes the batch under a best-effort PMD lock. The flush skips absent or non-huge entries, optionally clears non-leaf young state only when forced scanning is off and no notifiers are present, requires a successful young test-and-clear before accounting a folio, merges repeated folios, and preserves dirty indication across the batch.

PMD range traversal uses two passes so PTE tables are visited locklessly first and the PMD lock is taken only when young state must be cleared. It accounts leaf totals, ignores absent and huge-zero entries, applies non-leaf young gating and a sequence-indexed bloom filter unless forced scanning is set, records found versus added non-leaf statistics, carries forward bloom state to the next sequence on success, flushes any pending huge batch at the end, and restarts in a later VMA when the address range continues.

PUD range traversal iterates PUD slots, descends only into present non-leaf entries, delegates each subrange to the PMD walker, and truncates the current end at the containing PUD boundary when scheduling is needed or a per-walk batch limit is reached. It can cross into a later VMA and otherwise rounds the end upward; it reports completion distinctly from a request to resume, updating a next-address cursor to the later of the rounded end and the current VMA start on resume.

Reclaim eligibility combines memory control state, sizability, swappiness-derived minimum sequence, per-generation birth timestamp, and a global minimum time-to-live. Aging walks every memory control group on one node, computes protection, ORs reclaimability across groups with an initial fast path when no TTL is configured, and only when nothing is reclaimable attempts a best-effort out-of-memory invocation guarded by a trylock. The aging path asserts kswapd context.

Locking avoids sleeping or contended acquisition in table walks: the PMD batch flush uses only trylock and abandons the batch on failure, look-around requires the page table lock on entry and returns early when it is contended to avoid taking the LRU lock beneath it, generation migration holds the per-lruvec IRQ lock while moving bounded batches and drops it for scheduling between batches, the global enable switch nests cgroup then online-CPU then online-memory then a dedicated state mutex, and the OOM path uses only trylock.

Per-lruvec generation mode is a boolean with a strict list invariant: enabled mode requires all classic evictable lists empty, disabled mode requires all generation type-zone lists empty. Enabling migrates classic entries into generations and disabling migrates them back, each in bounded batches with rescheduling, after flipping a global switch branch and the core capability branch; other capability branches are toggled independently. Re-requesting the current mode is a no-op.

Sysfs exposes a TTL in milliseconds converted to and from jiffies with strict unsigned parsing, and an enable mask reporting core plus walker plus non-leaf capabilities as a small hex value. Writes accept a leading N for none, Y for all, or an unsigned mask; the core bit drives full state migration while other bits only toggle their capability branches.

Control objects are laid out as two read-write attributes grouped under one named sysfs group with null termination, a four-function sequential iterator for start stop next and show, and two file operation sets sharing open read seek and release where only the read-write set adds a write handler.

Sequential read iterates every memory control group and every memory node in order, skipping positions on start and advancing node then group on next, holding a per-file path-sized buffer. It prints a memcg header once per group with numeric identifier and path, then a node header, then one line per generation in a brief minimum-to-maximum window or a full bounded history window with size summed across zones and a marker for generations below the per-type minimum.

Write accepts a list of comma semicolon or newline separated commands each giving an operation character plus memcg identifier node generation and optional swappiness and option fields with whitespace tolerance and empty items ignored. It validates node online and memory state, resolves and identity-checks the memcg, defaults swappiness from current policy with an upper anonymous-only bound, dispatches plus to aging and minus to eviction, loops eviction in bounded batches until target count or minimum-sequence progress or a pending signal, and runs under reclaim-state plus no-reclaim allocation plus block plugging with a required walker context.

Full display expands each generation by protection tier and by anonymous versus file type, showing refault versus total averages for the newest sequence and refaulted versus evicted versus protected counters for older retained history selected by a history hash, with distinct placeholder versus reporting labels. It then optionally appends per-walker table statistics with separate current versus historical label sets depending on whether only one history generation is retained.

Walks must handle absent intermediate tables, huge-zero markers, notifier presence disabling fast young clearing, address wrap and range truncation, scheduler latency and batch exhaustion requiring resume, contended locks requiring abandonment, special copy-on-write mappings excluded from look-around, large folios requiring batched young and dirty evaluation, invalid nodes or unknown memcg identifiers, swappiness outside the supported range, future or too-recent sequences, interrupted eviction loops, and user copy or allocation failure on the command path.
A five-valued ordered enumeration distinguishes no memcg LRU action from head, tail, old, and young queue handling stages.

User-visible names comprise a sysfs group for generation controls with millisecond TTL and enable files, plus two debugfs files for brief read-write command access and full read-only inspection with conventional owner read-write versus read-only permission encodings.

Initialization enforces compile-time spacing between minimum and maximum generation counts and width capacity, warns without failing if sysfs group creation fails, creates the brief and full debugfs entries with the matching operation sets, and always reports success. An alternate build provides a generation aging entry that is a compile-time failure marker rather than a runtime implementation.
